title: Define a typed in-memory Fleet generation API
body:
## Outcome
Define and implement one typed `GenerationService` contract shared by the existing Fleet CLI, secrets, SSH, iroh and later PKI callers. Provide typed request/result and artifact classification, semantic algorithm/format identifiers, policy validation and injectable entropy/signer/writer seams. The API supports in-memory operation without implicit filesystem, provider or network I/O. Fleet remains the only CLI; do not add a parallel binary, CLI or resolver. Logical object IDs are stable opaque identities, distinct from mutable path/name and provider-native IDs.

## Current evidence and boundaries
V1 is the pinned existing system only—not a proposed implementation stage. This checkout has `fleet-secrets` as a broker-first/BWS name resolver (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs`), not a generation API; `fleet-registry` is std-only and the Fleet workspace already feature-gates domains (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-registry/src/lib.rs`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml`). Preserve `fleet secrets get/list`, its intentional secret-value stdout behavior, redacted errors/logs, and the connect variant dependency/size contract. Synthetic API work only; no PKI ceremonies or provider writes. Root private material is excluded from ordinary resolver refs, caches, prefetch, benchmark data and equality indices; signing and escrow require separate explicit capabilities.

## Acceptance and verification
1. In-memory API and CLI adapter produce the same typed metadata for one fixed synthetic request. 2. Typed errors distinguish invalid request, unsupported capability, entropy, signer and sink failures. 3. `Debug`, errors, tracing and receipts redact private values. 4. No default provider/network/disk side effect exists. 5. `fleet-connect` does not acquire generator dependencies and all existing variant/help smoke tests pass. 6. Renaming a path preserves opaque logical ID; two objects at different paths do not alias by name. Oracle: API/compile-time contract tests, deterministic fake RNG/signer/writer, and model-based rename tests. Inject entropy/sink failures and prove no success receipt; public-only signing and X.509 certificate-as-private-key refuse.

## Dependencies, rollout and recovery
No prerequisite; blocks GEN-02–GEN-10. Own the API crate/interface and tests only. High priority, size L, V2. Start Backlog; Ready only after variant constraints are validated. Roll back by removing/disabling optional feature; never regress existing secrets resolver behavior. All fixtures are synthetic.

title: Implement unbiased password and passphrase policy sampling
body:
## Outcome
Add password/token-string/passphrase generation using vetted OS CSPRNG entropy; fail closed on entropy failure. Separate candidate alphabets from required classes. Support short/standard/long/website/unrestricted policies, exclusions, configurable length and explicit byte/scalar/grapheme/normalization choices. Standard is conservative; Unicode/CJK/emoji remain explicit and versioned. Passphrases choose independently uniform indices from a versioned curated word list.

## Current evidence and boundaries
Fleet currently has no generator command; `fleet-secrets` resolves strings only. Implement through GEN-01 in the existing multicall surface. Do not test against live credentials, store generated secrets automatically, or claim arbitrary websites accept generated Unicode.

## Acceptance and oracles
For reduced finite alphabets, enumerate the valid output space and prove each output has equal sampling probability by construction; larger-domain property tests assert every result satisfies all constraints. Unsatisfiable policies fail before calling RNG. Entropy failure propagates; test lengths 16/32/64 and configured bounds, exclusion collisions, Unicode normalization and units. Entropy calculation must use actual effective sample space and constraints. Oracle: exhaustive reduced-domain enumeration plus property invariants; statistical tests are supplementary only. Negative tests reject empty/invalid alphabets, malformed charset files, impossible class requirements, below-floor entropy, invalid lengths and insecure deterministic production RNG. Logs/errors contain no result bytes.

## Dependencies, rollback and stage
Depends on GEN-01; owns sampler, policy API, CLI integration and tests only. High priority, L, V2. Synthetic test material only. Disable the feature on bias or redaction regression; existing Fleet commands remain unchanged.

title: Add versioned token encodings and UUIDv4 ID generation
body:
## Outcome
Separate random-byte token generation from encoding and from character-uniform base-N output. Add an explicit versioned registry for standard/nonstandard alphabets, UUIDv4 generation and parse/validation; `--uuid` is an alias for the dedicated UUIDv4 algorithm. ID types disclose collision, clock/order and information-leak properties; time-ordered IDs are not bearer tokens.

## Current evidence and boundaries
No Fleet generator registry exists; Fleet secret-name validation is a path-safety rule, not an ID format. This issue does not implement keypairs/signatures or provider sync.

## Acceptance and independent oracle
Round-trip all registered reversible formats; UUID bits conform to RFC 9562 and report 122 random bits; character-uniform sampling is unbiased for uneven byte-to-alphabet ratios, proved by reduced-domain enumeration. Parsers reject malformed or ambiguous case/padding per registry; batch names are unique. Use an independent RFC 9562 parser/reference implementation and exact enumeration. Negative tests reject unsupported aliases, false standard claims, entropy reported from encoded character count, and time-ordered ID use as secret token.

## Dependencies, rollback and stage
Depends on GEN-01 and shared sampler in GEN-02. Standard urgency, M, V2, Backlog. Registry versions may be deprecated but never silently reinterpreted. No external database or production writes.

title: Add typed key adapters with sign and independent verify
body:
## Outcome
Implement typed key adapters and in-memory generate/derive-public/fingerprint/sign/verify/inspect operations for explicitly supported algorithms and protocol-specific signature encodings. Verify keypair consistency before any sink. Never auto-discover an authorized root signer and never imply a certificate itself is a signing key.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet secrets currently handles named string values. `pkgs/id/src/lib.rs` has a separate sign-only-what-receipt-accepts contract (lines 54–103); do not copy or weaken it. This issue owns Fleet synthetic adapters, not PKI graph generation or production key operations.

## Acceptance and oracle
For each enabled algorithm, a synthetic fixture signs and independently verifies; wrong public key, altered message, unsupported digest/encoding and public-only signing fail. Fingerprint algorithm is explicit, generated keys round-trip, and feature tests prove unused providers are absent from connect variant. Oracle: OpenSSL 3.5+ and an independent Rust verifier where supported, with versioned standard vectors. Negative tests reject algorithm/format substitution, implicit signer lookup and claimed ML-DSA support without a passing verifier.

## Dependencies, rollback and stage
Depends on GEN-01. High urgency, XL, V2 before PKI use; Backlog. New dependencies/features must preserve Fleet size/profile contracts. Synthetic ephemeral keys only; disable adapter on independent verification failure.

title: Implement OpenSSH-native key generation and conversion policy
body:
## Outcome
Provide Fleet SSH key generate/inspect/get/import/export using OpenSSH-native formats: Ed25519 default, supported RSA-3072/4096 and P-256, with hardware-backed variants only when implemented. Reject obsolete DSA/short RSA by default; allow only a separately audited legacy policy. Do not describe classical SSH authentication as PQ-safe due to hybrid PQ key exchange.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet has no SSH identity domain; its existing proxy SSH transport is not an SSH-key lifecycle API. `pkgs/id` remains a separate product. This issue does not install files or perform remote changes.

## Acceptance and oracle
OpenSSH `ssh-keygen` and `ssh` parse/use every advertised format; derived public key/fingerprint matches OpenSSH; import/export preserves comments and parse semantics. Encrypted-key import cannot silently strip a passphrase; private export is explicitly approved. OpenSSH is the independent format/verification oracle. Negative tests cover tampering, incorrect passphrase, unsupported conversion, DSA/short RSA, public-only private export and unsupported algorithm claims.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends on GEN-01/04. High priority, size L, V2, Backlog. Synthetic keys only; no home-directory install or remote host access. Disable unsupported algorithm adapters rather than substitute.

title: Add version-pinned native iroh SecretKey and EndpointId adapter
body:
## Outcome
Pin iroh crate/API version and add native SecretKey generation, parsing/import, export, EndpointId derivation, inspection, and only documented sign/verify capabilities. Use versioned Fleet references/manifests; do not place secret bytes in metadata. Never equate EndpointId with X.509 trust, a CA identity, or authorization.

## Current evidence and boundary
`pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` uses iroh 1 / iroh-base 1; `pkgs/id/src/local.rs` uses native SecretKey and EndpointId; `pkgs/id/src/key_envelope.rs` has a version-1 passphrase-wrapped app format, and README documents `id key import/export`. Exact locked versions and serialization API must be checked when implementation begins. Do not modify `pkgs/id` or rewrite `.iroh-key`/`.iroh-key-client`.

## Acceptance and oracle
Native parser round-trips synthetic generated keys; derived EndpointId equals claimed ID; malformed/tampered/version-unknown/mismatched-ID inputs fail before writes. Oracle is the pinned native iroh parser/derivation plus versioned official docs at docs.rs. Test against `id`-format fixture read-only. Negative tests reject X.509 certificate as iroh identity and prevent automatic identity replacement.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends on GEN-01/04. Standard, L, V2, Backlog; optional Cargo feature. Active peer identity rotation is blocked for a separately approved lifecycle plan. Remove/disable adapter on compatibility regression; no active identity or provider mutation.

title: Adopt existing SSH and iroh keys through a read-only plan
body:
## Outcome
Adoption parses an explicit input read-only, validates native formats, derives fingerprints/identifiers, records provenance/relationships and emits an exact plan before any write. Preserve original bytes/comments and unknown fields in protected sidecars where authorized; never silently discard unsupported data or sync to providers.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet resolver is read-only by name. `id` already owns its encrypted import/export envelope and active identity; Fleet adoption must not replace it. No full personal-vault inventory or broad filesystem scan.

## Acceptance and oracle
Malformed/ambiguous inputs generate no writes; SSH fingerprint matches independent OpenSSH; iroh EndpointId matches native derivation; lossless source-sidecar export preserves exact original bytes; unknown fields are explicitly marked. `--dry-run` leaves filesystem/provider snapshot unchanged. Oracle: independent parsers, source hashes, and write-audit fixture. Negative tests reject private material in public sinks and reject unrecognized `id` envelope as raw iroh serialization.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends GEN-05/06 and OPS-01. Standard, L, V3, Backlog. Initial implementation is fixture-only/read-only. Apply requires a later explicit path and scoped approval; on failure retain source, remove only plan-owned additions after checking no intervening edits.

title: Install SSH files and merge configs with atomic recovery
body:
## Outcome
Install private/public SSH files separately after target-user, owner, mode, path, ACL and symlink checks. Merge `config`, `authorized_keys` and `known_hosts` structurally, preserving unrelated bytes, comments, order and user edits. Use staged same-filesystem writes, fsync, atomic rename and recoverable journal.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet has no SSH mutation domain. Do not modify `pkgs/id` paths or run against a real home directory in CI. This issue excludes remote hosts and host-key TOFU.

## Acceptance and oracle
Plan hashes all targets and is read-only. Private files default 0600 and `.ssh` 0700 subject to policy. Injected failures at each write/fsync/rename/readback leave original state or an exact recoverable partial receipt. Golden merge tests preserve unowned lines/comments; sudo target-user resolution is verified; unsafe symlink/traversal/owner/mode/ACL fails before any mutation. Oracle: independent parse/render fixtures plus filesystem snapshots and fault injection. Negative tests prove no wholesale overwrite, no new unverified host key, and no world-readable private key.

## Dependencies, rollback and urgency
Depends GEN-05/07, OPS-01/04. High, XL, V3, Backlog. Test with temporary roots only. Rollback checks hashes to avoid overwriting newer human edits; unsupported filesystem atomicity fails closed.

title: Stage and verify remote SSH rotation before retiring old access
body:
## Outcome
Implement a guarded rotation state machine: prove existing access and verified host identity; preflight target permissions; stage new public key beside old; verify a fresh login with new key; remove old authorization only after success and only if approved. Report per-host status and recover safely. SSH CA/principals/KRL remain distinct from X.509.

## Current evidence and boundary
No Fleet SSH remote control exists. Implement and test only in an isolated disposable SSH lab; no production host or broad unattended policy.

## Acceptance and oracle
MBT exercises every transition and retry; old access remains until new login succeeds; network loss, permission mismatch, timeout, rejected new key or partial update stops before removal; rollback does not overwrite intervening remote edits; incomplete run status is `partial` or `blocked`, never `rotated`. Approval binds host, user, fingerprints and plan hash. Oracle: disposable OpenSSH servers, actual client result, remote file hash/permissions, and reference state machine. Negative tests: changed host key, absent old-access proof, mismatched key, expired approval and remove-old-first all refuse.

## Dependencies, safety and rollback
Depends GEN-08, OPS-01/02/04/10. High, XL, V3. Production use is Blocked on explicit remote-change approval and verified out-of-band recovery access. Keep old key until new path and recovery are verified; stop and retain old access on any failure.

title: Define additive algorithm and format capability registries
body:
## Outcome
Create versioned typed capability registries for algorithms, key formats, signature encodings and sinks. Each adapter separately declares parse/encode/generate/sign/verify/public-derive/import/export and feature prerequisites; unknown or unsupported combinations fail closed. Additions never change existing IDs' meaning.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet's std-only registry and feature matrix are established patterns; Atlas uses versioned protocol boundaries. Do not create a second binary or pull all providers into connect. This issue defines extensibility; it does not implement every future OpenPGP/JWK/ML-DSA/HSM adapter.

## Acceptance and oracle
Schema declares stable ID/version, standard status, supported operations, feature prerequisites, dependency/client limits and independent test oracle. Duplicate IDs/ambiguous versions fail validation; runtime capability report matches compiled features; a synthetic adapter can be registered without changing core generation semantics. Oracle: schema conformance and artifact/feature-tree inspection. Negative tests reject capability advertised for a stub, silent format substitution, and dependency leakage into connect.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends GEN-01/04. Standard, L, V4, Backlog. Unknown registry version refuses; deprecate rather than reinterpret. No provider or production operation.

title: Define versioned operation plans, approvals and receipts
body:
## Outcome
Define versioned typed schemas for immutable plans, scope-bound approvals, run receipts, status and recovery references. Bind approval to plan hash, target/scope and expiry; separate private export, overwrite, remote change, provider write, retirement, root signing/custody and DNS/trust/deployment hazards.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet has version/capability reporting and a registry; current `fleet-secrets` is read-only and has no write journal. This issue owns schemas and validators only, not provider writers or live approvals.

## Acceptance and oracle
Rust types and JSON Schema share a golden corpus and preserve semantics through round-trip. Canonical plan IDs/hashes are stable; receipts redact sentinels; unknown schema/version, duplicate operation IDs, expired/misbound approval, malformed precondition and unsupported status fail closed. Oracle: independent JSON Schema and Rust validators plus property-based canonicalization. Negative: one-byte plan tamper, approval scope mismatch, and global `--force` must refuse; receipt contains no secret sentinel.

## Dependencies and rollback
No dependency; blocks OPS-02–OPS-06 and GEN-07+. High, L, V2, Backlog. Schema is additive/versioned; no real approval issued or mutation performed.

title: Add offline typed batch DAG validation
body:
## Outcome
Implement a versioned batch schema and offline validator for typed operations, explicit dependency DAGs, references, outputs/sinks, idempotency and compensation policy. Validation does not generate secrets or perform I/O.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet's proposed batch commands are design-only. Integrate with existing Fleet multicall and do not add a second command tool. This issue owns schema/parser/validator only.

## Acceptance and oracle
Require unique operation IDs, valid typed references, acyclic graph, deterministic topological order, size/depth limits, sink types and requested capabilities; output redacted plan and required scope list. JSON/YAML equivalent inputs canonicalize identically. Invalid version rejects before RNG or IO. Oracle: property-generated DAGs compared with reference topological evaluator; parser fuzzing. Negative: cycles, unresolved refs, duplicate IDs, path traversal, unsafe private output, and write disguised as validate all reject with zero side effects.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-01, GEN-01. High, L, V2, Backlog. Side-effect-free validator can be removed independently; no live operations.

title: Implement resumable plan apply verify and recover engine
body:
## Outcome
Create generic plan/apply/verify/recover orchestration with idempotency, durable journal-before-side-effect, per-step receipts and precondition rechecks. Multi-sink writes are a saga with partial status, never falsely atomic.

## Current evidence and boundary
No plan/apply/recover exists in current Fleet; current resolver is read-only. Implement generic engine with synthetic filesystem/test sinks only; no production provider adapter.

## Acceptance and oracle
Plan never mutates. Apply refuses stale hash, missing approval, changed revision or unavailable capability. Journal persists before effect. Inject crash after every step and prove retry does not duplicate completed work. Verify is read-only; recover observes current state and refuses to overwrite intervening edits. Oracle: MBT against state model plus crash/fault injection and filesystem snapshots. Negative: 403/timeout/partial listing is not deletion, unapproved apply has zero writes, and `--force` cannot bypass gates.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-01/02. High, XL, V2–V3, Backlog. Start with isolated temporary backends; production integrations require separate issues/gates. On partial failure report exact unresolved state; no fabricated rollback claim.

title: Build atomic recoverable file and archive transactions
body:
## Outcome
Provide safe Fleet filesystem sinks for separate public/private outputs and structured file merges, with validated owner/mode, staging, fsync, atomic commit where supported and a recoverable per-file journal. Reject path traversal, symlink escapes, archive bombs and duplicate names.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet has no generator sink. `pkgs/id/src/main.rs` uses CWD-relative identity/store files; do not modify them. Test Fleet implementation in temporary roots only, never operator home.

## Acceptance and oracle
Enforce private/public separation and modes; staged same-filesystem writes validate manifest/hashes before rename; injected failures at each boundary yield old state or explicit recoverable partial receipt; rollback checks for intervening edits. Oracle: filesystem snapshots, mode/owner checks and crash/failure injection; independent archive/path parser. Negative: symlink swap, traversal, case collision, disk-full/fsync failure, changed original, world-readable key and unsupported filesystem atomicity must refuse or report partial accurately.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-01/03; GEN-08 consumes this. High, XL, V3, Backlog. No real credential files; refuse unsupported atomicity rather than claim success.

title: Generate Fleet help manpages completions and schemas from registry
body:
## Outcome
Generate concise/long help, offline Markdown, man pages, Bash/Zsh/Fish/PowerShell completions and JSON/YAML schemas from Fleet's single typed command registry. Every command declares capability/profile, auth scope, side effects, sensitivity, errors and approval class; status is truthful.

## Current evidence and boundary
`fleet-registry` already drives full help and capability stubs for variants; v0.3 commands are proposed, not implemented. Preserve registry compatibility and do not advertise planned commands as available.

## Acceptance and oracle
Generation is deterministic; snapshots match actual CLI help in full/serve/connect variants; docs build fails on descriptor drift or missing examples/tests. Capabilities and completions reflect actual compiled surface. Oracle: registry descriptors plus golden help/shell parser tests. Negative: unavailable command does not autocomplete as supported, private values never appear, and aspirational command cannot be marked implemented.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-01 and existing fleet-registry. Standard, L, V2–V4, Backlog. Roll back generated output if parity fails; existing command surface remains stable.

title: Design and implement scoped Fleet agent skill installer
body:
## Outcome
Provide versioned agent skill bundles and a Fleet installer with explicit project/user/system scope, target-agent adapter, idempotent install/upgrade/remove and receipts. It must preserve user-authored AGENTS.md and settings.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet registry has no skills domain. This task's design does not edit repository or user AGENTS/skills; implementation only through future approved issue.

## Acceptance and oracle
Manifest declares schema/version/agent/path/ownership/checksum; dry-run, backup and atomic install; install is idempotent; upgrade/remove touches only files owned by manifest; unrelated human text survives. Fresh-context agent succeeds using installed skill and actual Fleet help without undocumented state. Oracle: manifest validation, before/after temp config trees and blind-run fixture. Negative: unknown agent, symlink/path escape, version mismatch, or existing unowned AGENTS.md overwrite must refuse.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-05/01 and GEN-05–GEN-09 docs. Standard, L, V4, Backlog. Test in temporary config roots only; this design makes no AGENTS.md or skill changes.

title: Generate client-specific public deployment kits and verify guides
body:
## Outcome
Generate per-client public-only kits with versioned manifest, hashes, selected chain/trust bundle, supported formats, tailored install/verify/rotate-overlap/remove instructions, privilege constraints and rollback. Compatibility and strict PQ-only trust profiles remain separate; private CA is not public WebPKI trust.

## Current evidence and boundary
Fleet has no PKI command or kit output; source lists target client families and limitations. This issue does not generate production certificates, publish DNS/HTTP, install trust, or package private keys.

## Acceptance and oracle
Synthetic kits contain only profile-approved public material and tested client instructions. Wrong profile cannot include forbidden anchors. Client matrix names exact version and marks unsupported/unrun honestly. Oracle: artifact hashes, OpenSSL plus Rust validator, and actual supported client verification. Negative trust tests reject classical paths under PQ-only profile, private-key inclusion, and unsupported client marked supported.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-01/05, GEN-04/10 and separate PKI manifest/engine issues. Standard, XL, V3–V4, Backlog. No install command executes; invalid kit is discarded as synthetic output.

title: Build synthetic Fleet-generated reference artifact evidence suite
body:
## Outcome
After generator/PKI implementation, use the built Fleet executable itself to create synthetic password/token/ID/SSH/iroh and reference PKI artifacts, then independently verify formats, secrecy, manifest counts and positive/negative crypto paths.

## Current evidence and boundary
No current generator or evidence pipeline exists. The spec requires a future tool-self-hosted demonstration. This issue uses synthetic/test keys only; never production root keys, provider writes or publication.

## Acceptance and oracle
Report pinned source revision, derived version, build variant, fixture identity, commands (without secret args), artifact hashes, verifier versions and outcomes. Fleet must be producer; independent tools are verifiers. When PKI is ready, reference matrix checks 20 CA pairs / 65 cert variants excluding leaves. Private bytes reside only in disposable isolated storage; receipt scanner finds no secret. Oracle: OpenSSL 3.5+, independent Rust verifier, OpenSSH, native iroh parser and typed expected matrix. Negative: tampered signature, wrong EndpointId, classical PQ-only path, unsupported key format, leaked private output, or network/provider access all fail.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends GEN-02–06, OPS-03/04 and separate PKI implementation. High, XL, V3 release gate, Backlog until producers exist. Opt-in local/CI synthetic suite; destroy fixtures; any unsupported case is reported, not substituted.

title: Maintain versioned crypto client and OS compatibility evidence matrix
body:
## Outcome
Maintain exact versioned interoperability evidence for OpenSSL/Rust, operating systems, browsers/JVM/mobile/embedded clients, OpenSSH and iroh. Distinguish tested, unsupported and untested; crypto path validation is separate from TLS key exchange.

## Current evidence and boundary
The spec proposes a broad client matrix; no v0.3 Fleet support claims have been demonstrated. Test disposable environments only; do not install global trust.

## Acceptance and oracle
Each matrix row records client/version, algorithms/formats/path policy, command, positive and negative outcomes, date and evidence hash. PQ-only tests validate all-ML-DSA path and reject classical path where verifier supports policy; SSH auth signatures and PQ KEX are separate. Oracle is each actual client's verifier and independently expected path model. Negative tests cover missing algorithms, malformed chains, wrong anchor, classical fallback, wrong host identity and SSH/X.509 confusion.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends GEN-04/05/06 and OPS-07/08. Standard, XL, V3, Backlog. Unsupported claims are removed/marked unknown; no system trust changes.

title: Specify production approval, custody and recovery gates
body:
## Outcome
Define a hazard-to-approval matrix and recovery gates for private export, overwrite, remote key change, provider write, retirement, root signing/custody, DNS/trust/deployment. Preserve the addendum's temporary explicit root custody set (encrypted laptop, authorized BWS project, authorized 1Password vault); R2 is research only and no general future-provider replication.

## Current evidence and boundary
No v0.3 write/custody API or live authorization has been verified by this design. Implement policy model and synthetic gates only; do not create/export/sync production roots, edit live vaults, change trust/DNS or deploy services.

## Acceptance and oracle
Each hazard has exact authority scope, plan-bound approval, preconditions, backup, independent readback, rollback and stop conditions. Root signing requires explicit signer ref, no ambient default; replication limited to approved destinations. Offline recovery design avoids circular dependency. Oracle: policy model and fault-injected state machine; every unapproved/stale plan produces zero mutations. Negative: global force, stale approval, missing signer or unapproved replica all refuse.

## Dependencies and lifecycle
Depends OPS-01/03 and separate PKI custody design. High, L, V2–V3. Production operations remain Blocked pending explicit applicable approval and tested custody/recovery.

title: Generate operator runbooks from verified Fleet interfaces
body:
## Outcome
Generate self-contained operator guidance for plan/apply/verify/recovery, private material protection, local adoption/install, SSH remote rotation and iroh identity lifecycle. Distinguish file generation from actual target-service activation and app identity from X.509 trust.

## Current evidence and boundary
Current Fleet and `id` READMEs exist, but v0.3 generator/SSH/iroh runbooks do not. This task edits Fleet documentation only after interfaces exist; it does not change AGENTS.md, `pkgs/id` policy or live operation.

## Acceptance and oracle
Docs carry requirement/source links, version, real command examples, scope/approval requirements, outputs, errors, failure/rollback and tested status. Every example runs against a test fixture or is prominently labeled unexecuted. Fresh-context operator completes a disposable walkthrough using only generated help/docs; no hidden state. Oracle: generated command descriptors and fixture transcript. Negative: absent command/capability is not invented, and docs never claim untested production readiness.

## Dependencies and rollback
Depends OPS-05/06 and GEN-05–GEN-09. Standard, L, V3–V4, Backlog. Documentation-only; revert generated pages if they drift from CLI.
